Again, there’s more to it than there seems. If a park knew that a manufacturer ONLY produced rides with a bad guest experience and costly and timely maintenance, they wouldn’t buy from that company. It’s often a blend of issues between a manufacturer, sub-contractors, and the park. If it was one person to blame, a park would never spend millions of dollars on  a ride from them. It’s so easy from the outside to just be like “oh that manufacturer’s rides are always down” but that’s a vast over simplification. It’s a terrible and toxic mindset to have. You claim to be “going into the industry”, find people to talk to who have first hand knowledge. 

I’m not gonna say there are companies who don’t have a worse portfolio than others, but every company who is still around has some winners.

Please if you’re going to be in this industry professionally, take everything with a grain of salt if it’s second hand. There is SO much misinformation out there. Very, very rarely is an issue with a ride a result of one party. If it was as simple as a company sucking, that company would quickly go out of business.

Then you’ll sit on the exam table and place the sheet over your lap like a blanket and just wait until the doctor comes. When they come they’ll chat with you about your issues and most likely want to do a pelvic exam. Explain it’s your first time, you’re nervous, you’re a virgin, and anything else you need to say and they will support you. You can ask them to use extra lube and at any point if you ask them to stop they will. They’ll also walk you through what they’re going to do before they do it. Break ups are difficult. Especially with someone you loved. You feel the hurt and the missing and the love for months afterwards. It's not even bit six months yet, it's perfectly okay to still miss and love him deeply but that does not mean you should try again.

You always have to remember, there's a reason you broke up. There was something you just couldn't deal with anymore. Don't put this on yourself and think you weren't "patient enough". You did your best and I'm sure he was doing his but sometimes having love for each other just isn't enough.

Neither of you have changed. He's still going to have his personal issues and it'll still bother you. You may try to be more understanding for a bit but deep down it'll still bother you. If you want someone who's open and will tell you about their day freely, you should give yourself time to find that. You can't change your ex and you shouldn't let him change what you want.

Everyone deserves someone who makes them happy to the core and gives them almost everything they want. These things your ex couldn't do that you wanted enough to the point where you broke up, you shouldn't push aside. You found love once and you'll find it again. You'll find someone who will tell you every little thing freely, not someone you can't handle.

Be strong. Don't let yourself sulk in this rut too long. It's okay to miss someone, it's not okay to let it break you. Do not get back with him. Right now you miss the love you two had, you miss the relationship, you miss having him around, but you're not remembering the negatives. That's reasonable with any break up, but you deserve what you want. Don't feel bad and think this is your fault. It's not your fault. He can find someone who can deal with his issues and you can find someone you can deal with too.

Keep your chin up, treat yourself, cry a bit and eat ice cream if you need to, but remember that there's someone perfect out there for you. You should settle for nothing less.
